commit_message:
feat(site): unify brand assets across app icon, favicons, and og-image

Extend generate-icon.mjs into the single source of truth for every Card Harbor logo raster: it now emits site favicons (ico, 32/16 png, apple-touch-icon), a transparent brand-mark png for in-page headers, and a scalable favicon.svg, all derived from the same brand mark used for the Electron app icon. Add generate-og-image.mjs to build the 1200x630 social card from the same mark instead of a hand-drawn one. Base.astro now links the full favicon set plus site.webmanifest and theme-color, and its schema.org logo points at the new logo.png. Legal.astro and index.astro swap their inline hand-coded brand-mark SVGs for the generated brand-mark.png so every surface renders the same logo.

Constraint: Generated PNG/ICO assets must be regenerated via node scripts/generate-icon.mjs and node scripts/generate-og-image.mjs whenever src/renderer/src/assets/card-harbor-mark.png changes; they are not hand-editable.
Confidence: medium
Scope-risk: moderate
Not-tested: Favicon/og-image rendering not verified in an actual browser or social-card unfurler after the asset regeneration.

findings.issue: favicon.svg generation manually rebuilds a rounded rect with BACKGROUND and a hand-computed radius instead of reusing the existing backgroundSvg() helper that already does exactly this composition step, duplicating logic that lives two functions above it

icoFrom() and pngFrom() are near-identical: both call renderBadge, then fs.writeFileSync + console.log('wrote', ...) with the same message shape; that write+log pair is also repeated inline for favicon.svg and brand-mark.png (4 copies total of the same two lines)

header comment is a mini design-doc (drop-shadow rationale, crop survival, run instructions) that mostly restates what the code below already shows; only the drop-shadow alpha hack actually needs a why-comment

favicon.svg draws rounded background rect then overlays badge256 image which already bakes in same background+radius (from renderBadge compositing onto backgroundSvg) - redundant double-background, harmless since image fully covers rect.
findings.fix: Skip separate rect and just embed badge256 image, or skip background compositing in renderBadge call for badge256 and let SVG rect provide it.

findings.issue: Deshadow logic re-encodes extractChannel(3) alpha as PNG buffer then joinChannel(alpha) onto rgb buffer; unverified this sharp pipeline produces correct alpha-adjusted image (no test/run evidence in diff).
findings.fix: Run script once and visually confirm mark has no dark halo before merging; add inline note if empirically tuned.

historical.message: feat(brand): standardize logo across site and social onto one mark The Card Harbor logo had diverged: the app/taskbar icon and og-image used the detailed harbor mark, while the site favicon and the inline header SVGs used a different, simplified redraw. Unify everything onto the single brand mark (src/renderer/src/assets/card-harbor-mark.png) that the app icon already uses. - generate-icon.mjs: promote from app-icon-only to the single source for every logo raster. In addition to build/icon.{ico,png} it now emits the full site favicon set (favicon.ico, favicon-16x16, favicon-32x32, apple-touch-icon, a favicon.svg badge), a square logo.png for schema.org Organization.logo, and a square, transparent brand-mark.png for in-page headers. brand-mark.png is padded to a square canvas so a fixed square CSS box renders it without distortion. - generate-og-image.mjs (new): rebuilds site/public/og-image.png from the same mark, de-shadowing it for the white card. Centered lockup (mark + one-line name + tagline) survives a square center-crop so Slack/Discord/ iMessage thumbnails stay readable. - Base.astro: wire the full favicon set + web manifest + theme-color, and point Organization.logo at /logo.png (square raster) instead of the SVG. - index.astro, Legal.astro: replace the inline simplified brand-mark SVG in the header with so headers use the real mark. - site.webmanifest (new): PWA manifest referencing the generated icons. Constraint: keep one brand mark as the single source; the app icon already uses it, so the site and social assets move to it rather than the reverse. Rejected: keeping a separate simplified favicon/header glyph (the whole point was that it read as a different logo); vectorizing the raster mark (it is a raster brand asset, so favicon.svg wraps it and og/headers use PNGs). Directive: standardize the logo, seeing different versions across app, site, and SEO. Confidence: high Scope-risk: narrow Not-tested: no automated coverage; verified by running both generators, building the site (6 pages), inspecting the built head for the favicon set / manifest / theme-color / JSON-LD logo, and eyeballing the mark at favicon, header (28px, undistorted), and og-image sizes plus a 240px square crop. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context)
